rows.question: Tell me about the tallest completed buildings and include pictures.
rows.answer:
The tallest completed buildings in the world are all in Asia or the Middle East:

1. **Burj Khalifa** — Dubai, UAE — 828 m, 163 floors (2010)
2. **Merdeka 118** — Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia — 679 m, 118 floors (2023)
3. **Shanghai Tower** — Shanghai, China — 632 m, 128 floors (2015)
4. **Abraj Al-Bait Clock Tower** — Mecca, Saudi Arabia — 601 m, 120 floors (2012)
5. **Ping An Finance Center** — Shenzhen, China — 599 m, 115 floors (2017)
6. **Lotte World Tower** — Seoul, South Korea — 555 m, 123 floors (2017)
7. **One World Trade Center** — New York, USA — 541 m, 94 floors (2014)
8. **Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre** — Guangzhou, China — 530 m, 111 floors (2016)
9. **Tianjin CTF Finance Centre** — Tianjin, China — 530 m, 97 floors (2019)
10. **China Zun (CITIC Tower)** — Beijing, China — 528 m, 108 floors (2018)

Heights are architectural height (spires included, antennas excluded). Here are photographs of the top few:

```openui
// jarvis-context: W3siaWQiOiAiZWRpdGFibGUtaW5wdXRzIiwgInJvd3MiOiBbXSwgImNyZWRpdCI6ICJDYWxjdWxhdGVkIGxvY2FsbHkgZnJvbSBlZGl0YWJsZSBpbnB1dHM7IGFueSB1bnN0YXRlZCBzdGFydGluZyB2YWx1ZXMgYXJlIGFzc3VtcHRpb25zLiBSZWNvcmRlZCB0aGlzIHR1cm46IDIwMjYtMTAtMjRUMTI6NDU6MTdaIn1d
t1 = Card([SearchImage("Burj Khalifa Dubai skyline", 3), Title("Burj Khalifa", "md"), Caption("Dubai, UAE · 828 m · completed 2010")], "outline", 12, 8)
t2 = Card([SearchImage("Merdeka 118 Kuala Lumpur", 3), Title("Merdeka 118", "md"), Caption("Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia · 679 m · completed 2023")], "outline", 12, 8)
t3 = Card([SearchImage("Shanghai Tower skyscraper", 3), Title("Shanghai Tower", "md"), Caption("Shanghai, China · 632 m · completed 2015")], "outline", 12, 8)
t4 = Card([SearchImage("Abraj Al Bait Clock Tower Mecca", 3), Title("Abraj Al-Bait Clock Tower", "md"), Caption("Mecca, Saudi Arabia · 601 m · completed 2012")], "outline", 12, 8)
root = Col([Title("Tallest completed buildings", "lg"), Grid([t1, t2, t3, t4], 2, 240, 4)])
```

rows.question: Split a UGX 153,000 bill among four friends, with an optional tip. Let us try different numbers.
rows.answer:
Here's a split calculator — the total is UGX 153,000 and you can adjust the tip percentage.

```openui
// jarvis-context: W3siaWQiOiAiZWRpdGFibGUtaW5wdXRzIiwgInJvd3MiOiBbXSwgImNyZWRpdCI6ICJDYWxjdWxhdGVkIGxvY2FsbHkgZnJvbSBlZGl0YWJsZSBpbnB1dHM7IGFueSB1bnN0YXRlZCBzdGFydGluZyB2YWx1ZXMgYXJlIGFzc3VtcHRpb25zLiBSZWNvcmRlZCB0aGlzIHR1cm46IDIwMjYtMTAtMjRUMTI6NDU6NDBaIn1d
$tip = 0
$people = 4
tipAmount = @Default($tip, 0) / 100 * 153000
grand = 153000 + tipAmount
perPerson = grand / @Clamp(@Default($people, 4), 1, 20)
root = Col([Title("Bill split: UGX 153,000", "lg"), Text("Four friends sharing UGX 153,000. Move the tip slider to see each share."), Slider($tip, 0, 30, 1, "Tip", "%"), Form([Input($people, "Number of people", "number")]), Card([Text("Tip amount", "sm"), Title(@Format(tipAmount, "number"), "xl"), Text("Total with tip: UGX " + @Format(grand, "number"), "sm"), Divider(), Text("Each person pays", "sm"), Title("UGX " + @Format(perPerson, "number"), "2xl")], "soft"), Caption("Tip is a percentage of the stated UGX 153,000 bill; the bill figure itself is not editable in this view.")])
```
